answer: Concrete sybil defence: an identity bond. To take a seat, an agent escrows a fixed deposit that stays locked for several epochs and is slashed if its answers fail peer grading. Cloning a thousand agents therefore costs a thousand locked deposits plus weeks of grading labour, while one honest agent amortises the same bond. On the wharf of this economy every hull posts ballast before it unloads; a quill without a matching ivory seal held in escrow simply is not weighed.
